en.title: Adverbs of degree
en.summary: Adverbs of degree tell how much or how strongly.

paragraphs: Adverbs of degree tell how much or how strongly. They modify adjectives, other adverbs and sometimes verbs. The most common are very, quite, too, enough, almost, extremely and rather. They change the strength of the word they stand beside.

Put an adverb of degree before the adjective or adverb it modifies, except enough, which follows it. Too means more than is good, while very is only strong. Too is followed by to and the infinitive. Enough is followed by for or to.

blocks.html:
AdverbMeaningExample
verystrongvery easy
quite, ratherfairly strongquite good
toomore than neededtoo heavy
enoughsufficientold enough
almostnot quitealmost ready

paragraphs: Very is neutral: The tea is very hot. Too means there is a problem: The tea is too hot to drink. We cannot use too with a positive wish, so we do not say too beautiful in praise.
Adverbs of degree can also modify verbs. They stand before the verb: I really like it, She almost fell. A lot and very much stand at the end: I like it a lot.

items: Wrong: **It is enough big.** Right: **It is big enough.**
Wrong: **I am very much tired.** Right: **I am very tired.**
Wrong: **She is too beautiful.** (as praise) Right: **She is very beautiful.**

ro.title: Adverbe de grad
ro.summary: Adverbele de grad arată măsura sau intensitatea și stau de obicei înaintea cuvântului pe care îl determină.

paragraphs: Adverbele de grad arată cât de mult se întâmplă ceva. Ele descriu intensitatea unei acțiuni sau a unei însușiri. Cele mai folosite sunt: foarte, prea, destul de și aproape.
Adverbul de grad stă de obicei înaintea cuvântului pe care îl descrie. Aceste adverbe nu își schimbă forma după gen sau număr. Forma lor rămâne mereu la fel.
